note: An inline endpoint 55.000 m from its arc under SPEC 3.3.3, which a conforming reader must refuse, dropping the link per SPEC 6.2 - not the endpoint, which would leave a malformed link, and not the chain, which would be disproportionate. The arc runs north to south on purpose, and this is the least obvious property in the pair: do not tidy it to match its ascending twin. A refusal case cannot catch a model that over-reads, because over-reading also refuses. Descending puts the segment start at high latitude and the query at low, so a reader taking the cosine of the segment's start latitude under-reads it at 36.824 m and accepts a document the format refuses. That is the more dangerous direction, because a reader that silently accepts bad geometry is worse than one that complains about good geometry, and nothing else in the corpus covers it. The thirteen degrees are deliberate for the same reason as the accept case: the error is a percentage and a realistic arc hides it. The expected message deliberately omits the measured distance, because the number a reader reports depends on its arithmetic and a conforming implementation differing in the last metre should not fail. What is pinned is that the endpoint was refused and the tolerance named.
